name: top-reaction-5col-table
prompt:
Place a small label below the arrow:
“allenylation conditions”

Use only generic line-angle chemistry placeholders. Do not invent an exact molecular structure, catalyst structure, ligand structure, stereochemistry, reaction condition, yield, or enantiomeric excess.

Below the reaction scheme, create five equal-width vertical catalyst-family columns labeled:

1. Cu
2. Pd
3. Au
4. Rh/Ir
5. Other metals

Each column should contain four compact sub-blocks:

- Catalyst / ligand
- Representative case
- Key selectivity
- Synthetic note

For “Representative case”, show a generic substrate-to-allene reaction placeholder and a blank field such as:
“up to ___ % ee”

For text fields, use short dotted placeholders rather than long paragraphs.

At the bottom, add a full-width ribbon labeled:

“Shared themes & outlook”

Inside this ribbon, include four concise icon-and-label modules:

- scope
- mechanism
- utility
- future directions

The figure should communicate the central reaction, metal-centered classification, representative chemistry, selectivity, and common conclusions within approximately 20 seconds.

Make the layout reusable for other overview figures in the allene chemistry field.

name: center-radial-classification
prompt:
Use only abstract chemical line placeholders. Do not invent or approximate exact chemical structures, ligands, mechanisms, stereochemical assignments, reaction conditions, yields, or ee values.

From the central panel, create five balanced branches leading to outer catalyst-family panels:

- Cu
- Pd
- Au
- Rh/Ir
- Other metals

Each outer panel should contain three short information rows:

- typical catalyst system
- representative transformation
- key message

Use simple academic icons:
- flask for catalyst system
- reaction arrow for transformation
- star for key message

Use dotted placeholder lines for information that will later be filled from the review outline.

Around the outer boundary, place four small global-theme callouts:

- reactivity control
- enantioselectivity
- substrate scope
- applications / outlook

Connect these themes using a subtle dashed oval or open boundary, without making the figure look like the supplied reference images.

The figure should be symmetric, easy to scan, and suitable as a reusable metal-centered overview template for allene chemistry reviews.

name: route-map-start-strategy-result
prompt:
CENTER PANEL:
Create five horizontal catalyst lanes:

- Cu
- Pd
- Au
- Rh/Ir
- Other metals

For each lane, arrange three sequential information boxes:

1. Catalyst / ligand
2. Reaction pattern
3. Key result

Use small chevron arrows between the boxes.

The “Catalyst / ligand” box may contain an abstract ligand icon such as:
L–M–L

The “Reaction pattern” box should show only a generic alkyne/alcohol-to-allene transformation.

The “Key result” box should contain short placeholders for:
- enantioselectivity
- yield
- scope highlights

Do not insert fabricated catalyst structures, mechanisms, chemical structures, yields, or selectivity data.

RIGHT PANEL:
Title:
“Outcome”

Subtitle:
“Enantioenriched allenylated products”

Include a generic chiral allene product and three compact outcome boxes:

- reactivity
- selectivity
- synthetic value

Use a bold arrow from the central metal strategies panel to the outcome panel.

BOTTOM BAND:
Title:
“Challenges & outlook”

Include four modules:

- mechanism
- broader scope
- milder systems
- scalability

The final figure should read clearly from starting materials and scientific challenges, through metal-dependent strategies, to reaction outcomes and future directions.

name: module-cards-crosscut-sidebar
prompt:
Below the reaction strip, arrange five tall rounded cards:

- Cu
- Pd
- Au
- Rh/Ir
- Other metals

Each card should have a colored header and contain four mini-sections:

1. Design logic
2. Representative case
3. Selectivity
4. Take-home point

Use the following types of placeholder descriptions:

Design logic:
“Key idea of ligand/catalyst design and activation mode.”

Representative case:
“Catalyst/ligand, allenyl source, conditions, substrate type.”

Selectivity:
“Typical enantioselectivity, diastereoselectivity, and yield range.”

Take-home point:
“One-line key takeaway or advantage.”

Use dotted lines for information that will later be filled by an intelligent planner.

On the far right, add a narrow vertical panel titled:
“Cross-cutting issues”

Include four modules:

- Scope
- Mechanism
- Late-stage utility
- Future opportunities

At the bottom of the sidebar, add:
“Time window: 2020–2025”

At the bottom of the main card area, add a short abbreviations line:
“APA = propargyl alcohol-type compound; [M] = metal catalyst.”

The final layout should be modular, easy to populate automatically from keywords and an outline, and suitable for general use in allene mini-reviews.

name: tree-metal-classification
prompt:
Below the reaction, create a central dark rounded node labeled:

“Metal-centered classification”

From this central node, draw five major branches leading to circular metal nodes:

- Cu
- Pd
- Au
- Rh/Ir
- Other metals

Below each metal node, place three vertically stacked leaf boxes:

1. Substrate class
2. Stereocontrol mode
3. Synthetic highlight

In “Substrate class”, show a generic alkyne–alcohol motif.

In “Stereocontrol mode”, use an abstract metal–ligand or chiral-pocket diagram, not an exact transition state.

In “Synthetic highlight”, use a simple icon and a short placeholder such as:
“Key result or advantage”

At the bottom, connect the five metal branches into a shared rounded conclusion box titled:

“General lessons”

Inside, place four icon-and-label sections:

- Catalyst choice
- Selectivity logic
- Scope considerations
- Outlook and opportunities

The figure should resemble a scientific taxonomy tree rather than a biological tree, and should be reusable for different allene reaction themes.

name: why-strategy-what
prompt:
SECTION 2:
Title:
“Metal strategies”

This should be the largest central section.

Create five horizontal modules labeled:

- Cu
- Pd
- Au
- Rh/Ir
- Other metals

Each module contains three columns:

- Catalyst system
- Representative case
- Selectivity logic

Catalyst system may contain:
- L* ligand
- metal source
- additives
- solvent

Representative case should contain a generic propargyl alcohol-to-allene reaction.

Selectivity logic should use short placeholder items such as:
- axial induction
- ligand pocket
- steric control
- migratory sequence
- chiral environment
- transition-state bias

These labels are conceptual placeholders and must not be treated as factual claims for every metal family.

Do not fabricate real catalyst structures, catalytic cycles, exact mechanisms, structures, yields, or selectivity data.

SECTION 3:
Title:
“What do we learn?”

Show several generic chiral allene product motifs and four summary blocks:

- Scope
- Selectivity
- Applications
- Future outlook

Use bold arrows between Sections 1, 2, and 3.

At the bottom, add a shared summary band with three concise messages:

- recent metal strategies
- mechanistic and ligand-design insights
- future opportunities

The result should look like a review-level conceptual overview rather than a reaction database table.

name: mosaic-infographic
prompt:

- Au

- Other metals

1. Catalyst
2. Chemistry
3. Selectivity
4. Highlight

Catalyst:
- chiral ligand
- metal source

Chemistry:
- allenyl source
- reaction mode

Selectivity:
- ee
- dr
- regioselectivity

Highlight:
- key innovation
- representative scope
- notable example

Use abstract catalyst icons and generic molecular motifs only.

Add a smaller support tile on the lower left titled:
“Key trends”

Include:
- broader substrate scope
- higher stereoselectivity
- diverse allenyl sources
- greener conditions
- mechanistic insights

Add a smaller support tile on the lower right titled:
“Outlook”

- new catalyst systems
- untapped reactivity
- enantiodivergent control
- late-stage applications
